definitions.gloss: preserved food; long-lasting food; emergency rations
definitions.explanation: Food that has been processed or prepared to last a long time without spoiling. Includes canned goods, dried foods, freeze-dried meals, and disaster preparedness supplies.

examples.japanese: {非常用|ひじょうよう}の{保存食|ほぞんしょく}を{備|そな}えている。
examples.english: I keep emergency preserved food on hand.

examples.japanese: {保存食|ほぞんしょく}の{賞味期限|しょうみきげん}を{定期的|ていきてき}に{確認|かくにん}しよう。
examples.english: Let's regularly check the expiration dates on preserved food.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}の{保存食|ほぞんしょく}は{味|あじ}も{種類|しゅるい}も{豊富|ほうふ}で、{災害|さいがい}{時|じ}でもおいしく{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: Modern preserved food comes in a wide variety of flavors, making it possible to eat well even during disasters.

notes:
A compound of {保存|ほぞん} (preservation, storage) and {食|しょく} (food).

In Japan, {保存食|ほぞんしょく} is particularly associated with disaster preparedness ({防災|ぼうさい}). Households are encouraged to keep a supply of preserved food for earthquakes and other emergencies.

Traditional Japanese preserved foods include {漬物|つけもの} (pickles), {干物|ひもの} (dried fish), and {梅干|うめぼ}し (pickled plums).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {保存食|ほぞんしょく}を{備蓄|びちく}する (to stockpile preserved food)
- {非常用|ひじょうよう}{保存食|ほぞんしょく} (emergency preserved food)
- {長期|ちょうき}{保存食|ほぞんしょく} (long-term preserved food)
